SECTION MENU
City Council meets regularly to discuss and make decisions on matters affecting the community.
Regular Council meetings are usually held on the third Tuesday of each month at 6:00 p.m. These meetings are live-streamed on the City’s Facebook and YouTube channels, allowing residents to watch from home.
Committee of the Whole meetings are generally held on the first Tuesday of each month at 3:00 p.m.
From time to time, special Council meetings may be scheduled as needed.
Meetings are held in the City Hall Council Chambers, located at 325 Farr Drive, Haileybury, unless another location is announced in advance.

Called on an as-needed basis

Committee of the Whole meeting held on the second Tuesday of the month at 3:00 p.m.

Council may change or cancel the date of any meeting by resolution. If a meeting date falls on a Public Holiday when City Hall is closed for business, the meeting will be scheduled on the next business day.
Any Council and/or Committee of the Whole meeting may be held using a hybrid format (in-person and electronic participation), in accordance with Section 238 of the Municipal Act, 2001, and the City’s Procedural By-law. Electronic participation is limited to members of Council, staff, and registered delegates.
Viewing Council Meetings
Members of the public are welcome to attend the open session portions of meetings in person.

Regular and Special Council Meetings (open sessions) are live-streamed on the City’s Facebook page and YouTube channel, with recordings archived on those platforms.
Note: Live streaming and video recordings are not available for Committee of the Whole meetings.
Council Meeting Agenda and Council Package
Prior to each meeting, members of Council receive an electronic Council Package, which may include:
The meeting agenda
Previous Council minutes

Draft by-laws
The agenda and Council Package are available to the public and are normally posted on the website on the Friday prior to a Regular Council meeting.
If you are unable to locate a document or experience difficulty accessing a link, please contact the Clerk’s Department at clerk@temiskamingshores.ca.

Participate in a Council Meeting
Delegations provide members of the public with an opportunity to make a presentation to Council of up to 10 minutes.
Delegations at Regular Council meetings must relate to matters within the jurisdiction and authority of local government.
Delegations at Committee of the Whole meetings must relate to an item included on the published agenda.
Requests to appear as a delegation must be submitted to the Clerk’s Department by completing a Delegation Request Form or by emailing clerk@temiskamingshores.ca, no later than 4:30 p.m. on the Wednesday prior to the meeting. Submission of a request does not guarantee approval.
If a delegation request is approved, a written copy of the presentation must be provided to the Clerk by 4:30 p.m. on the Thursday prior to the meeting.
For additional information, please refer to the Delegation Protocol.

Whereas Section 238 of the Municipal Act, 2001, S.O 2001, c 25 as amended, requires
that every municipality shall pass a procedural by-law for governing the calling, place and
proceeding of meetings and any of its committees; and
Whereas Council considered Administrative Report CS-007-2023 at the March 7, 2023
Regular Council meeting, and directed staff prepare the necessary by-law to Adopt a new
Procedural By-Law, repealing By-Law 2008-160, as amended and all its associated
amending By-Laws for consideration at the March 7, 2023 Regular Council meeting; and.
Whereas Notice as prescribed by By-Law 2004-022, being a By-Law to establish
procedures for public notice for the matter of the Procedural By-law was given by way of
an advertisement in the Temiskaming Speaker on the March 1st and 8th, 2023, in addition
to Notice being provided on the City of Temiskaming Shores website;
Now therefore the Council of the Corporation of the City of Temiskaming Shores hereby
enacts the following as a by-law:
1. That the Council for the City of Temiskaming Shores hereby adopts the “Procedural
By-law”, a copy of which is attached hereto as Schedule “A” and forming part of this
by-law.
2. That this by-law may be referred to as the “Procedural By-law”.
3. That the following by-laws be hereby repealed on the effective date of passing and
replaced entirely with “Schedule A” hereto: Procedural By-Law 2008-160, as
amended; in addition to By-Laws 2009-058, 2009-113, 2010-130, 2011-014, 2014-
101, 2015-231, 2020-035, 2021-156, 2022-089.
4. That any former By-law adopted to establish a committee of council or adopting a
Terms of Reference in which makes reference to the provisions set out in Procedural
By-law 2008-160, as amended shall be hereby considered replaced with the
provisions set out in Schedule A to By-law 2023-022, attached hereto.
5. That the Clerk of the City of Temiskaming Shores is hereby authorized to
make minor modifications or corrections of a grammatical or typographical nature to
the by-law and schedule, after the passage of this by-law, where such modifications
or corrections do not alter the intent of the by-law.
6. That this by-law shall come into full force and effect on the date of final passing.

1. DEFINITIONS
In this by-law:
1.1 "Ad Hoc Committee" means a Committee established by Council to review a
specific matter and once the Committee has reported with respect to its findings
and recommendations, the Committee is automatically dissolved.
1.2 "Call the question" means that the vote on the Motion shall be taken.
1.3 "Chair" means the Mayor or the Presiding Officer of a meeting.
1.4 "City Manager" means the City Manager of the Corporation.

Submissions are to be sent electronically to:

If submitting a physical copy, they may be mailed to:

Project Information
1. Purpose
The Corporation of the Township of Terrace Bay is seeking quotations for the supply and installation of
a new security camera system to replace its existing dated system.
The Township is seeking a reliable, modern and expandable security camera system that includes all
equipment, software, installation and support required for operation, together with as many priority
cameras as can reasonably be provided within the available project budget. The system must also
allow additional cameras or locations to be added in the future.
2. Project Objectives
The Township’s objectives for this project are to:
• Replace the Township’s dated camera system with a modern digital system;
• Provide a complete and operational system, including all required equipment, software, licensing,
installation and support;
• Replace as many of the Township’s priority existing cameras as reasonably possible within the
available project budget;
• Provide secure and user-friendly access to live and recorded footage;
• Identify any internet, networking and ongoing service requirements associated with the proposed
system; and
• Establish a system that can accommodate additional cameras and municipal locations in the future.
3. Project Locations and Priorities
The current project includes existing cameras at the following municipal locations:
• Terrace Bay Community Centre;
• Terrace Bay Swimming Pool; and
• Simcoe Plaza, where two existing cameras are located.
Priority will be given to replacing the existing cameras at these locations, together with the equipment,
software and infrastructure required to provide a complete and operational system.
One existing outdoor camera operates separately from the system being replaced and can already be
accessed remotely. Replacement or integration of this camera is considered a lower priority and may
be proposed if the available project budget permits.
The final number of cameras replaced will be determined based on the proposed system requirements,
site conditions and available project budget. Proponents may recommend alternative camera
placements where they would provide more effective coverage.
Future expansion to the Cultural Centre, Tourist Information Centre, Lighthouse or other municipal
locations is addressed in Section 5.
4. Scope of Work
The successful proponent will complete the following work:
• Review the existing camera locations, equipment and site conditions at the Terrace Bay Community
Centre, Terrace Bay Swimming Pool and Simcoe Plaza;
• Recommend an appropriate system design and camera placement;
• Supply and install a complete digital security camera system, including cameras, recording and
storage equipment, software, licensing, cabling, mounts, power supplies and all other required
components;
• Replace or remove existing equipment where required for the new installation;
• Identify any internet connection, networking, subscription, licensing or other ongoing service
requirements and associated costs;
• Configure and test the completed system;
• Provide authorized Township staff with secure access to live and recorded footage;
• Provide system documentation, warranty information and staff training;
• Include as many priority camera replacements as reasonably possible within the available budget
while ensuring the base quotation provides a complete and operational system; and
• Provide a prioritized expansion plan with separately itemized pricing for any priority camera
replacements that cannot be included in the base quotation.
The proposed system must be capable of accommodating additional cameras and municipal locations
without requiring premature replacement of the central recording, storage or management equipment.
5. Optional and Future Services
Proponents may provide separate pricing or planning information for the following:
• Replacement or integration of the newer independently operated outdoor camera;
• Future security camera coverage at the Terrace Bay Cultural Centre, Tourist Information Centre,
Terrace Bay Lighthouse or other municipal locations;
• Public-facing HD livestream coverage at Terrace Bay Beach or the Terrace Bay Lighthouse;
• Livestream capability at the arena for tournaments and events; and
• Livestream capability at the curling club for bonspiels and events.
These items must be identified and priced separately and must not reduce the equipment, installation
or priority camera replacements included in the base quotation. This information is requested for future
planning purposes and may not form part of the work awarded under this RFQ.
6. Site Reference Information
The Township has prepared a Google Earth reference map identifying the existing security camera
locations and providing supplementary site photographs.
For security reasons, access to the map will be provided to proponents upon request. Proponents may
request access by contacting:
Stacy Moffat, Special Projects Coordinator
spc@terracebay.ca
The Terrace Bay Community Centre currently has the following Tbaytel internet services:
• Fibre 1 Gbps service for the Township’s secure office network; and
• 75 Mbps service for free community Wi-Fi.
Proponents must identify whether the proposed system can use either existing connection or requires a
separate dedicated internet service.
The information in this section is provided for reference purposes only. Proponents are responsible for
verifying camera locations, existing infrastructure, site conditions and access requirements.
7. Deliverables
The successful proponent will provide:
• A fully installed and operational digital security camera system, including all required cameras,
recording and storage equipment, software, licensing, materials and other components;
• Configuration and testing of all installed components;
• Secure access to live and recorded footage for authorized Township staff;
• Confirmation of the system’s internet and network requirements, including whether a dedicated
internet service is required;
• System documentation, including camera locations, equipment details, operating instructions,
licensing information and warranty information;
• Training for designated Township staff; and
• A prioritized expansion plan with separately itemized pricing for any priority camera replacements or
future locations not included in the base quotation.
All deliverables must be completed no later than December 11, 2026.
8. Pricing Requirements
Proponents must provide clear, itemized pricing for the base quotation, including:
• Cameras and related equipment;
• Recording, storage and system management equipment;
• Software and licensing;
• Materials;
• Labour and installation;
• Travel and associated expenses;
• Configuration and testing;
• Training; and
• Any other costs required to provide a complete and operational system.
Proponents must also identify:
• Any internet, networking or connectivity requirements and associated one-time or recurring costs;
• Any licensing, subscription, maintenance or other recurring costs;
• Separate pricing for any priority camera replacements not included in the base quotation;
• Separate pricing or planning information for the optional and future services identified in Section 5;
and
• Warranty coverage and the cost of any optional extended warranty or support services.
The Township has an available 2026 project budget of $15,000, excluding HST, and is seeking a
complete and operational system within or as close as reasonably possible to this amount.
All pricing shall be provided in Canadian dollars.
9. Submission Requirements
Proponents shall provide:
• Relevant experience and qualifications;
• Proposed system design and approach;
• The number, type and proposed location of cameras included in the base quotation;
• Details regarding recording, storage, system access and future expansion capacity;
• Proposed project timeline;
• Warranty and post-installation support information;
• A prioritized expansion plan for cameras or locations not included in the base quotation;
• References for at least two comparable projects; and
• Completed pricing information in accordance with Section 8.
10. Evaluation
Submissions will be evaluated based on:
• Relevant experience and qualifications;
• Understanding of the project scope;
• Proposed system and approach;
• Equipment, coverage and overall value provided within the available budget;
• Capacity for future expansion; and
• Cost.
The Township is not obligated to accept the lowest-priced submission and may select the submission
that provides the best overall value.
11. General Conditions
The Township reserves the right to:
• Accept or reject any or all submissions;
• Request clarification or additional information from any proponent;
• Adjust the final combination of cameras and locations in consultation with the preferred proponent,
based on the available budget; and
• Cancel this RFQ without awarding a contract.

1. Introduction
1.1 Purpose
This report presents the findings of the site inspection and existing system review carried out at
Tillsonburg Regional Airport (CYTB) on 20 July 2026. The work was performed under the quotation issued
by Arc & Spark Electric on 26 June 2026 and approved by the Town of Tillsonburg.
The review was undertaken to establish the existing conditions relevant to the proposed installation of
four Precision Approach Path Indicator (PAPI) units held by the airport, and to determine whether that
installation is feasible.
The review addresses the electrical and site conditions relevant to the installation. Where those
conditions are conditioned by matters outside the electrical scope, this report identifies them.
1.2 Site Visit
The visit took place on Monday, 20 July 2026, beginning at 08:00. Site access and orientation were
provided by airport staff. The review covered the airport electrical service and panel, the airfield lighting
control equipment, the runway lighting installation, the four PAPI units held in storage, and the ground
conditions in the areas relevant to installation.
1.3 Scope of This Report
This report presents existing conditions, assesses those conditions against the requirements of the
proposed installation, and provides conclusions on feasibility. It identifies the inputs required to proceed
to detailed electrical design. Photographic documentation is provided in Appendix A.
The following were carried out as part of this review:
• Inspection of the electrical service, meter, main breaker and distribution panel
• Review of the existing airfield lighting power and control system, including circuit configuration,
control method, and measurement of existing circuit loading
• Assessment of the capacity of the existing circuits to accommodate the additional PAPI load
• Identification of candidate power sources, connection paths and routing constraints
• Inspection of the four PAPI units
• Visual assessment of ground and surface conditions
1.4 Obstacle Clearance
Obstacle assessment was not included in the quoted scope of this review and has not been charged for.
It is included because the electrical review was undertaken to establish whether a PAPI installation can
proceed, and whether a system can be sited at a given runway end is governed first by obstacle clearance.

Tillsonburg Regional Airport is a registered aerodrome. This report applies Transport Canada TP312, 5th

TP312 is applied because it is the recognized Canadian standard for the design of the systems concerned,
and because the geometric and configuration requirements it sets out are the basis on which the
equipment functions as intended. Where this report identifies a departure from TP312, it states the
technical position against the standard applied. It is not a statement regarding the aerodrome's regulatory
obligations.

2. Summary of Findings
Obstacle clearance
The trees on the Runway 26 approach, approximately 635 m from the threshold, reach approximately 299
m elevation against a threshold elevation of approximately 271 m. The Obstacle Protection Surface
required for a PAPI or an APAPI at the Runway 26 end is penetrated by roughly 8 to 9 m.
The same trees sit close to the 5 percent non-instrument approach surface for Runway 26 defined in
TP312 Table 4-1(a) for Aircraft Group Number I. Screening indicates a clearance of roughly 1 to 2 m. The
elevation data was acquired in 2025, and the stand continues to grow. The Canada Flight Supplement
carries a published caution for trees east of Runway 26.
Screening of the Runway 08 approach shows no comparable obstacle.
These findings are based on the Ontario lidar-derived Digital Surface Model, which is a screening dataset
and not a survey.
Electrical service
The airport is supplied at 120/240 V, single-phase, three-wire, through a 200 A main breaker. Peak service
demand can only be established from the utility's metering records, as it varies seasonally and with airport
activity. The distribution panel has no free breaker positions.
Airfield lighting system
The airfield lighting is a parallel 120 VAC system. There is no constant current regulator and no series
circuit.
Four branch circuits serve the runway lighting. Measured currents at maximum brightness are 7.07 A, 5.31
A, 2.10 A and 2.94 A, against breaker ratings of 20 A, 15 A, 15 A and 15 A, respectively. All four circuits are

a reduced voltage of approximately 51 VAC obtained through variable autotransformers, triggered by a
photocell. The lights are otherwise off.

Council Meeting Schedule

Starting January 2026, Council will meet monthly. Regular Council Meetings will be held on the fourth Tuesday of each month beginning at 9:30 a.m.

This change follows a successful 2025 pilot project, during which Council and staff observed improved agenda preparation timelines, more efficient internal workflows, and enhanced opportunities for Council to balance meeting preparation with other municipal responsibilities.

Meetings will occur on the fourth Tuesday of each month. Council meetings are scheduled to begin at 9:30 a.m., with the Open Session commencing at that time. Closed Session matters are generally considered near the end of the Open Session Agenda, unless otherwise indicated on the Agenda cover page.

The location and start time of each meeting will be confirmed on the published Agenda cover page.

In a municipal election year, the October meeting may be cancelled or rescheduled at Council’s discretion to avoid conflict with Election Day.

Written Submissions:
Members of the public may submit written comments related to items on the Agenda. To be included as part of the official meeting record, submissions must be received by the Clerk’s Office no later than 3:00 p.m. two business days prior to the scheduled meeting. Please note that any information submitted, including contact details, will form part of the public record.

Heritage Vaughan Committee Report
DATE: Wednesday, August 26, 2026 WARD(S): 2
TITLE: PROPOSED DEMOLITION OF THE CONTRIBUTING PROPERTY
AT 8204 KIPLING AVE. WITHIN THE WOODBRIDGE HERITAGE
CONSERVATION DISTRICT
FROM:
Vince Musacchio, Deputy City Manager, Planning and Infrastructure Development
ACTION: DECISION
Purpose
Seeking an evaluation and recommendation of staff-preferred Option A, from the
Heritage Vaughan Committee for Council approval, for the relocation and conservation
of the Moody-Darker House as previously approved by Council on Feb. 22, 2023, in
response to the received application for the proposed demolition of the existing 1 ½-
storey residential structure at 8204 Kipling Ave. The subject property is designated
under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act in the Woodbridge Heritage Conservation
District, as shown on Attachment 1. This heritage application is concurrent to the
ongoing Ontario Land Tribunal appeals filed by LCT Investment Group Ltd. for the lands
at 8158, 8196 and 8204 Kipling Ave., Tribunal file no. OLT-21-001869.
Item 1
Page 1 of 10
Page 3
Report Highlights
 The property is Designated Part V under the Ontario Heritage Act and is
identified as a contributing property in the Woodbridge Heritage Conservation
District.
 Staff does not endorse the demolition of heritage property and recommend
that the structure be relocated and conserved per the previously Council-
approved proposal on Feb. 22, 2023.
 Staff have outlined three options with varying conservation strategies and
mitigation of impacts in the ‘Analysis and Options’ section of this report, which
are not included in the Cultural Heritage Impact Assessment Addendum found
at Attachment 3. Option A for the relocation and conservation of the Moody-
Darker House is staff’s preferred option, while Option C for the
documentation, salvage, and commemoration, and ultimately the demolition
of the heritage resource, is the least preferred.
 The proposed new development on the remaining lands will be subject to a
future Heritage Vaughan review and Council Approval under section 42 of the
Ontario Heritage Act.
Recommendations
1. That Heritage Vaughan evaluates the merits of the following Options: A)
relocation and conservation; B) selective relocation and rehabilitation; or C)
documentation, salvage and commemoration (full demolition), for their
recommendation to Council for approval under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage
Act.
2. That pursuant to Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act, Heritage Vaughan
recommends approval be subject to the following conditions:
a. That prior to issuance of the heritage permit for demolition (including
relocation), the owner shall enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
pursuant to section 37 of the Ontario Heritage Act, to the satisfaction of the
City, which shall be registered on title to the lands at 8158, 8196 and 8204
Kipling Ave. at the owner’s sole cost and expense, to:
i. secure Council’s approved option and
ii. provide timeline and security for the above.
b. That the Deputy City Manager, Planning and Infrastructure Development be
the delegated authority to negotiate and execute a Heritage Easement
Agreement on behalf of the City.

Background
The subject property is a triangular-shaped parcel located between Kipling Avenue to
the east and the Canadian Pacific Railway Company lands to the west, which intersect
to the south of the property. The subject property includes an amalgamation of three
properties: 8158, 8196, and 8204 Kipling Ave. The site currently consists of open grass
fields (8158 and 8196 Kipling Ave.) and a vacant 1 ½-storey vernacular Gothic Revival
structure built circa 1880 (8204 Kipling Ave.), known as the “Moody-Darker House.”
The latter is situated on the northeast limit of the property, fronting the Meeting House
Road and Kipling Avenue intersection. The property is designated under Part V of the
Ontario Heritage Act and is a contributing property in the Woodbridge Heritage
Conservation District, within the Kipling Avenue North character area.
During its meeting on Feb. 22, 2023, Council adopted without amendment the
recommendations in Item 13, Report No. 9, of the Committee of the Whole for the
relocation, renovation, and new construction at 8204 Kipling Ave. Within that 2023
application, the Moody-Darker House was proposed to be relocated to the south of the
amalgamated property site within a park space, to accommodate the construction of 3-
storey townhouses fronting Kipling Avenue and a 5-storey midrise building fronting the
railway. A Cultural Heritage Impact Assessment was prepared by Parslow Heritage
Consultancy Inc., dated April 2021, in support of this application, Attachment 2.
In response to the requested review of the proposed plans and building design of the
current application from LCT Investment Group Ltd. for 8158, 8196 and 8204 Kipling
Ave., cultural heritage staff provided comments dated Dec. 19, 2025, stating that, per
Section 6.2.4 of the Woodbridge Heritage Conservation District Plan, “Buildings and
structures located within properties that are listed as contributing to the Woodbridge
Heritage Conservation District Heritage Character shall not be demolished and shall
remain in-situ within their existing context. The house located at 8204 Kipling Ave. is a
contributing property to the Woodbridge Heritage Conservation District.”
In June 2026, cultural heritage staff received a heritage demolition application from
Goldberg Group, on behalf of the owner, and advised the applicant that a Heritage
Review would be required for a complete application under the Ontario Heritage Act. A
Cultural Heritage Impact Assessment Addendum was subsequently prepared by
Peninsula Heritage Ltd., dated June 16th, 2026, as shown on Attachment 3.
Staff issued the Notice of Receipt on July 8, 2026, and under Ontario Heritage Act
section 42, Council has to make a decision on the application within 90 days of the
issuance of the Notice of Receipt, which will be October 6, 2026.

Vaughan Official Plan 2010
Section 6.3.2.5 of Vaughan Official Plan states “That a demolition permit for a building
or part of a building within a Heritage Conservation District shall not be issued until
plans for a replacement structure have been submitted to the City and Council has
approved the replacement structure and any related proposed landscaping features in
accordance with the relevant Heritage Conservation District Plan, the Vaughan Heritage
Conservation Guidelines and the policies of this Plan”
Considering that the planning application has been appealed to Ontario Land Tribunal,
Council is no longer the approval authority for the planning application. Staff therefore
have decided to separate the demolition application from the new construction
application under the Ontario Heritage Act and currently only request Heritage
Vaughan’s recommendation to Council regarding the status of the contributing building
located at 8204 Kipling Ave.
The new construction application on the remaining lands at 8158 and 8196 Kipling Ave.
will be brought forward for Heritage Vaughan review and Council approval at a future
date.

Analysis and Options
The applicant has proposed the demolition of the existing 1 ½-storey heritage building
built circa 1880, the Moody-Darker House.
Staff note that the current proposal’s default strategy for the demolition of the heritage
property, as outlined in the Cultural Heritage Impact Assessment Addendum,
Attachment 3, does not sufficiently review the feasibility of other mitigative measures
with the exception of documentation and salvage strategies. As a result, staff outline
three options for conservation strategies below, for purposes of Heritage Vaughan’s
evaluation and recommendation for Council approval:
Option A – relocation and conservation (staff’s preferred option)
This option is preferred and recommended by staff as it is consistent with the heritage
application previously approved by Council on Feb. 22, 2023, complies with the
Item 1

Page 6
Woodbridge Heritage Conservation District Plan, and is in keeping with good
conservation practices.
As the current site plan also includes a dedicated open space at the southernmost
portion of the subject site, similar in size as the prior heritage application’s Site Plan,
staff can endorse the relocation of the Moody-Darker House to the open space similar
to the previously approved heritage application by Council or within the development.
The relocation and conservation strategy should be outlined in a forthcoming
Conservation Plan.
Option B – selective relocation and rehabilitation
This option is considered a thoughtful compromise between staff’s preferred relocation
strategy (Option A) and the current proposal’s demolition (Option C). Staff could
endorse the selective relocation of the Moody-Darker House’s notable exterior
elevations’ heritage attributes and their rehabilitation as a commemorative feature within
the currently proposed open space’s landscape design at the southernmost portion of
the subject property. This option would enable the partial conservation of the Moody-
Darker House for valuable interpretation of the property’s history, while enabling the
new development and maintaining the heritage resource’s unique ‘sense of place’ as
well as cultural heritage value for its future residents.
The above-noted option has not been provided as an alternative to demolition by the
heritage consultant in the Cultural Heritage Impact Assessment Addendum. The scope
of documentation, salvage, and conservation strategy should be outlined in a
forthcoming Conservation Plan.
Option C – documentation, salvage and commemoration (demolition)
Staff do not endorse this option, as it is currently presented within the Cultural Heritage
Impact Assessment Addendum, shown on Attachment 3. Should this option be
Council’s preferred option, staff recommend that the existing heritage resource be
documented, its materials found to be in good condition salvaged, and the property
commemorated with salvaged materials and a plaque. The scope of documentation,
salvage, and commemoration should be outlined in forthcoming Documentation and
Commemoration Plans.
Woodbridge Heritage Conservation District Plan, 2009
The Woodbridge Heritage Conservation District Plan provides objectives, guidelines
and intervention notes for all repairs, alterations, additions and new development of
contributing properties. All proposed works within the boundary of the district must

adhere to the Plan. The following is an analysis of the objectives and guidelines which
apply to the subject property:
5.1 Objectives
1. Identify, document, maintain and restore the unique village character of
Woodbridge.
2. Conserve contributing buildings, landscapes, monuments and streetscapes.
3. Ensure new designs contribute to the Woodbridge heritage character.
4. Manage any development or redevelopment proposed within the district, in a
manner that is sensitive and responsive to all aspects necessary to ensure the
protection and conservation of the heritage resources, in order to maintain the
village character of the Woodbridge District.
5. Ensure individual heritage structures and landscapes are maintained, and new
development or redevelopment sensitively integrated, as part of a
comprehensive district.
6. Maintain Woodbridge as both a local neighbourhood and a destination for
residents of Vaughan and beyond.
7. Support a welcoming, interesting pedestrian environment by encouraging
pedestrian amenities and by maintaining human-scales development and
connections to adjacent neighbourhoods.
8. Involve area residents, property and business owners, and interested
individuals in the ongoing evolution of the Heritage Conservation District.
Section 6.2.4 Demolition of Contributing Buildings
Buildings and structures located within properties that are listed as contributing to
the Woodbridge [Heritage Conservation District] Heritage Character shall not be
demolished and shall remain in-situ within their existing context.
The contributing property at 8204 Kipling Ave., the Moody-Darker House, is currently
proposed to be demolished. Staff cannot endorse the demolition of the heritage
property, as this strategy does not comply with the Woodbridge Heritage Conservation
District Plan’s objectives. As a result, staff recommend pursuing the conservation and
commemoration strategies outlined in Options A or B above, with the relocation strategy
outlined in Option A being the preferred option.
Section 6.2.2 Conservation Guidelines
 conserve and protect the heritage value of each heritage resource. Do not
remove, replace, or substantially alter its intact or repairable heritage
attributes.

BY-LAW NO. 022-2023
As Amended by By-law No. 044-2023, By-law No. 019-2024 and By-law No. 008-2025
Being a by-law to repeal and replace By-law No. 058-2019
being a by-law to govern the proceedings of the Township of
Wainfleet Council, the conduct of its Members and the
calling of meetings.
WHEREAS Section 238 (2) of the Municipal Act, S.O. 2001, c. 25, as amended,
provides that every municipality and local board pass a procedure by-law for governing
the calling, place and proceedings of meetings;
WHEREAS Section 238 (2.1) of the Municipal Act, S.O. 2001, c. 25, as
amended, provides that the procedure by-law shall provide for public notice of meetings;
NOW THEREFORE the Council of the Corporation of the Township of Wainfleet
HEREBY ENACTS AS FOLLOWS:
1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 Act – means the Municipal Act, S.O. 2001, c. 25, as amended.
1.2 Agenda – means the order of business setting out the matters to be considered
at a meeting.
1.3 Deputy Mayor – means a Member who has been appointed in accordance with
this by-law to act for a designated period of time in the absence of the Mayor.
1.4 Amendment – means to alter or vary the terms of the main motion without
materially changing its purpose.

be followed for a Committee, in all proceedings of Council and its Committees,
the following rules and regulations shall apply and be observed and shall be the
rules and regulations for the order and dispatch of the business in Council and
the Committees thereof:
(a) Parliamentary Authority
All matters, Points of Order or questions of procedure arising and not
provided for in the rules contained herein shall be in accordance with
“Meetings Procedures, Parliamentary Law and Rules of Order for the 21st
Century” by James Lochrie.
(b) Distribution of this By-law
Following a regular or new municipal election, the Clerk shall provide each
Member with a copy of this by-law, including amendments thereto.
(c) Amendments to this By-law
No amendment, alteration or addition to this by-law shall be made unless
due notice has been given setting forth the proposed amendment,

shall not be permitted in the Council Chambers during a Meeting.
(e) Electronic Devices
All cell phones, pagers, radios, etc. shall be switched off, non-audible or
muted during a Meeting with the exception of pagers and similar devices
carried by members of the fire service or other first responders, in the
interest of public safety.

3.1 Members are required to comply with the provisions of the Municipal Conflict of
Interest Act, R.S.O. 1990, c.M.50, as amended.
3.2 Disclosures of Interest
3.2.1 Where a Member, either on his or her own behalf or while acting for, by, with or
through another, has any Pecuniary Interest, direct or indirect, in any matter and
is present at a Meeting of the Council or local board at which the matter is the
subject of consideration, the Member:
a) Shall understand and comply with their legal obligations under the
prevailing conflict of interest legislation;
b) Shall, prior to any consideration of the matter at the Meeting, disclose the
interest and the general nature thereof;
c) Shall not take part in the discussion of, or vote on any question in respect
of the matter; and
d) Shall not attempt in any way whether, before, during or after the Meeting
to influence the voting on any such question
3.2.2 At a Meeting in which a Member discloses an interest, or as soon as possible

as Schedule “A”)

Tuesday following the date of the commencement of the term of the new
Council. The opening ceremonies for the Inaugural Meeting shall be as
determined by the Clerk.

5.4 Regular Meetings shall be held in the Council Chambers at the Municipal

the Members, summon a Special Meeting for the purpose and at the time

(c) The Clerk shall provide all Members and the public with a minimum of

Council of the Municipality of Wawa meets twice a month. Regular and Corporate Planning meetings are held on the 1st and the 3rd Tuesday of the month except for July, August and December which are held on the 2nd Tuesday of the month. Meetings begin at 6:30 p.m.

Download the application here: Delegation Request Form
or a paper copy cab be picked up at the Municipal Office at 40 Broadway Avenue.
Applications can be submitted electronically by email to the Clerk at moneill@wawa.cc, or in writing to Municipality of Wawa, 40 Broadway Avenue, PO Box 500, Wawa, ON P0S 1K0, and must outline the reason for the presentation as per the Procedural By-Law. Memorandum from M. Weatherbie, Senior Manager of Government Relations & Grants, dated August 21, 2026 regarding Skills Development Fund Capital Stream - GROW Pathway - Fire Training Tower and Education Campus
 Recommendation:
Whereas the Town of Whitby has submitted an application to the Province of Ontario’s Skills Development Fund (SDF) Capital Stream - GROW Pathway for the Whitby Fire Training Tower and Education Campus, which would expand the Fire Training Tower currently under development through the addition of an Education Centre, enhanced training infrastructure, and advanced training technology; and,
Whereas the proposed project will create a comprehensive municipal training campus to support classroom instruction, practical skills development, technical rescue training, and simulation-based learning for firefighters and other emergency service personnel; and,
Whereas Whitby Fire and Emergency Services currently relies on training facilities located in neighbouring municipalities to deliver portions of its training programs, creating operational and scheduling challenges and limiting local training capacity; and,
Whereas the proposed Education Centre and associated training infrastructure would enable the Town to increase local training capacity, enhance operational readiness, improve firefighter recruitment and onboarding, and support ongoing professional development for current and future emergency service personnel; and,
Whereas the project is intended to serve as a long-term municipal asset supporting workforce development and public safety, while creating opportunities for collaborative training with emergency services partners and training organizations across Durham Region and beyond; and,
Whereas the proposed project is expected to increase access to modern training opportunities using classroom facilities, virtual reality and simulation technology, vehicle extrication training infrastructure, and purpose-built training space designed to meet evolving emergency response requirements; and,
Therefore, be it resolved:
That the Town of Whitby Council endorses the Town’s application to the Ontario Skills Development Fund Capital Stream - GROW Pathway for the Whitby Fire Training Tower and Education Campus;
That Council supports the use of the proposed facility for firefighter recruit training, certification and recertification, incident command training, emergency response exercises, technical rescue and vehicle extrication training, and ongoing professional development for Whitby Fire and Emergency Services personnel;
That Council confirms the expanded facility is expected to improve local training capacity, reduce reliance on external training venues, strengthen operational readiness, support emergency services workforce development, and provide long-term benefits to residents through enhanced emergency preparedness and public safety;
That Council acknowledges the regional value of the proposed facility and supports its use, where appropriate, to facilitate training opportunities for emergency service partners, neighbouring municipalities, and other eligible workforce development and public safety training providers; and
That this resolution be provided to the Skills Development Fund Capital Stream - GROW Pathway by email to SDFCapitalProgram@ontario.ca as evidence of Council’s support for the proposed training facility.

From: Melissa Weatherbie, Sr. Manager

Date: August 21, 2026

Subject: Skills Development Fund Capital Stream -
GROW Pathway - Fire Training Tower and
Education Campus
Council is being asked to endorse the Town’s application to the Skills Development
Fund (SDF) Capital Stream - GROW Pathway and approve a resolution of support for
submission to the Province as part of the application review process. This memo
provides an overview of the funding opportunity, summarizes the Whitby Fire Training
Tower and Education Campus project submitted in 2025, and outlines why a Council
resolution is needed to demonstrate municipal support and the anticipated community,
operational, and regional benefits of the proposed project.
The Ontario Skills Development Fund (SDF) Capital Stream - GROW Pathway supports
capital projects that build, expand, renovate, or modernize training facilities to increase
workforce training capacity in high-demand sectors. Municipalities are eligible
applicants, and approved projects may receive provincial funding for up to 49% of
eligible project costs. In July 2025, the Town of Whitby applied to the 2024-2025 round
of funding for the Whitby Fire Training Tower and Education Campus. The project would
expand emergency services training capacity, support workforce development, and
strengthen local and regional emergency preparedness.
The proposed Whitby Fire Training Tower and Education Campus builds on the existing
Fire Training Tower project by adding an Education Building and complementary
training infrastructure. The expansion includes dedicated classroom and training space,
an auto-extraction training pad, training equipment storage, mobile washroom facilities,
and advanced training technology such as virtual reality simulation software, laptops,
and tablets. Together, these investments would create a comprehensive training
campus to support modern firefighter and emergency services training.

If approved, the funding would help increase local training capacity, reduce reliance on
external training facilities, and support more predictable access to training for Whitby
Fire and Emergency Services. The expanded campus is expected to accommodate
approximately 250 trainees annually and serve as a long-term municipal asset
supporting workforce development, operational readiness, and public safety for Whitby
and the broader Durham Region.
The Town’s application seeks approximately $2.54 million in provincial funding,
representing the program’s maximum contribution of 49% of eligible project costs. The
total eligible project cost is estimated at $5.19 million. The remaining $2.65 million
would be funded through the existing approved capital budget.
The SDF Capital Stream - GROW Pathway permits eligible project costs incurred after
the launch of the program in June 2023 to be considered for funding reimbursement,
subject to provincial approval and the terms of the Transfer Payment Agreement. This
provision may allow the Town to include eligible project planning, design, and other
approved capital-related expenditures already incurred as part of the Fire Training
Campus project. The Town has updated the province on the status of the current Fire

To: Members of the Accessibility Advisory Committee
From: Donna Van Wyck,

Date: March 14, 2022
Re: Multi-Year Accessibility Plan Annual Status Report 2021
Recommendation:
That the Multi-Year Accessibility Plan Annual Status Report 2021 be received for
information and forwarded to the Executive Committee for approval and posting on the
Bruce County website.
Background:
Ontario Regulation 191/11: Integrated Accessibility Standards 4(1) requires designated public
sector organizations to establish, implement, maintain and document a multi-year
accessibility plan, which outlines the organization’s strategy to prevent and remove barriers
and meet its requirements under this Regulation.
In addition, Section 4(3) requires those same designated public sector organizations to
prepare an annual status report on the progress of measures taken to implement the
strategies of the multi-year accessibility plan and to post the status report on their website.
The attached Annual Status Update to the Multi-Year Accessibility Plan, is an update on
goals and accomplishments for each for each of the accessibility standards for 2021.
Multi-Year Accessibility Plan
Annual Status Report
2021
1
Accessibility Status Report
This Accessibility Status Report is the annual update on the progress of measures taken to improve
accessibility and implement the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA) and the
Integrated Accessibility Standards Regulation (IASR).
This status report includes the accessibility initiatives that were completed in 2021 to implement
the strategies outlined in Bruce County’s Multi-Year Accessibility Plan.
Bruce County’s Commitment to Accessibility
The Corporation of the County of Bruce is committed to eliminating barriers and improving
accessibility for persons with disabilities in a manner that respects dignity, independence
integration and equal opportunity.
Bruce County recognizes the diverse needs of all our residents and customers and will respond by
striving to provide services and facilities that are accessible to all. Bruce County is committed to
meeting the needs of people with disabilities in a timely manner and will do so by preventing and
removing barriers to accessibility and meeting accessibility requirements under the Accessibility for
Ontarians with Disabilities Act.
The County will promote accessibility by ensuring that compliance is met for all regulations made
under the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005. To ensure that timelines are met,
the County will establish, implement and maintain a multi-year accessibility plan. The plan will
outline the County’s strategy to prevent and remove barriers to people with disabilities.
AODA Compliance
The County completes an AODA compliance report for the Province every two years. A compliance
report was completed and submitted to the Province on December 17, 2021.
The County reported non-compliance for the Information and Communications Standard, for
accessible websites and web content. Though we are non-compliant, the County will continue to
work towards compliance with the requirements of the AODA for accessible websites and web
content.
2021 Accessibility Status Report
The 2021 Accessibility Status Report includes the County of Bruce's commitment to removing
barriers to our programs, services and facilities and the progress we have made on the actions to
meet the AODA.
2
1. Accessible Customer Service
The County is committed to offering excellent accessible customer service by making sure all
members of the public receive a fair customer service experience that meets their needs. Ongoing
compliance with the customer service standard includes the training of new hires as part of their
orientation and volunteers who interact with the public on the County’s behalf.
Accomplishments:
• Continued to review customer feedback and take appropriate action.
• Continued to comply with the requirements of the Customer Service Standard, including
implementing the Accessibility policy and training staff on an ongoing basis.
2. General Requirements
The County is committed to developing, implementing and maintaining policies governing how we
achieve or will achieve accessibility through meeting our requirements under the accessibility
standards referred to in the Integrated Accessibility Standards Regulation.
Accomplishments:
• Reviewed the County's Multi-Year Accessibility Plan in preparation of the Annual Status
Report which will be posted on the County’s website.
• Continued to incorporate accessibility features into our procurement or acquisition of goods,
services and facilities where applicable.
• Continued to train all staff and volunteers on the Integrated Accessibility Standards
Regulation (IASR), which now includes the Customer Service Standard and the Ontario
Human Rights Code (OHRC) as it pertains to people with disabilities.
• The County’s Accessibility Policy guides efforts to achieve compliance with AODA
requirements and establishes the County’s core accessibility principles. The Policy’s
statement of commitment affirms the County’s commitment to meet the accessibility needs
of all people. The Policy was updated in 2017 to include revisions related to service animals
and support persons that were effective July 1, 2016.
3
3. Information and Communication
The County is committed to ensuring information and communications are available and accessible
to people with disabilities.
Accomplishments:
• Continued to make sure that content on websites, intranet sites and print communications
are created in a way that considers accessibility.
• A statement is included on the County’s website informing users that documents are
available in an accessible format.
• Staff continue to receive annual training on creating accessible documents.
• Continued to provide accessible formats and communication supports as requested.
• A feedback form is provided on the website, and we continue to make sure processes for
receiving and responding to feedback are accessible.
• All Library branches continue to provide accessible materials and communications supports.
In addition, the library has several accessible materials and resources available including but
not limited to large print books; audio books; large font keyboards (available in most
branches); trackball mouse (available in all branches); assistive technology on all computers
(i.e., magnifier, high contrast, narrator – all included with Microsoft software); online access
to resources, policies, online request for items
• Siteimprove (an auditing tool) scans the County’s website content for accessibility and
identifying errors. Web Content Ambassadors work towards correcting any identified errors.
• eScribe is used for the provision of electronic meeting management software. This provides
for the utilization of common software for reports, agendas and minutes with a dedicated
portal for access to agenda items. The portal will provide an easily accessible manner for
Council, staff and the public to find and view any relevant items. The implementation of
this software has been a step in the right direction towards full compliance with the
Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act.
• eScribe provides closed captioning for the videos of Council and Committee meetings.
• A Guide to Accessible Documents was created in 2021 for use by staff.
• In 2022 staff will have access to on-line training tutorials for creating and checking
accessible Word and PDF documents to ensure they are AODA compliant.
• Interested Staff attended a “Understanding the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities
Act (AODA) and Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG)” webinar on October 4, 2021
• Staff participated in virtual accessible document training in October and November, 2021
• Staff continue to monitor and correct departmental templates to accessible formats
4
4. Employment
The County is committed to inclusive and accessible employment practices that ensure the
processes of recruiting, hiring, communicating with, and retaining employees who have disabilities
is inclusive.
Accomplishments:
• Continued to inform applicants and employees of accessible hiring practices and policies.
• Continued to provide individualized workplace emergency response information to
employees who require one because of a disability.
• Continued to support employees who were absent from work because of a disability, through
our return-to-work process.
• Continued to include a statement on all job postings that we accommodate the needs of
qualified applicants under the Human Rights Code in all parts of the hiring process.
• Advise candidates when scheduling interviews/testing that we have an Accommodation in
the Workplace Policy for persons with disabilities and ask them if they require an
accommodation for their interview and or test.
• Inform all new employees in their offer letter about the County’s Accommodation in the
Workplace Policy.
• Inform all new and existing employees of the County’s policy for supporting employees with
disabilities.
5. Design of Public Spaces Standard
The County is committed to identifying, removing and preventing barriers in public buildings and
spaces by making sure that new construction and major changes to existing features do not create
any new barriers.
As a large public sector organization, the Design of Public Spaces Standard only applies to new
construction and planned redevelopment on or after January 1, 2016.
Ontario’s Building code has been amended to include enhancements to accessibility in buildings.
As of January 1, 2015, new construction and renovations will be subject to updated accessibility
requirements.
If a public space is temporarily disrupted or not functioning, the public will be notified in a variety
of formats about the scope of the disruption.
5
Accomplishments:
• Continued to make sure that major changes to existing features meet or exceed the
requirements of the Design of Public Spaces Standard.
• Continued to train staff on the Design of Public Spaces Standard which is included with the
IASR training. This training is done on-line through the County’s attendance management
software as part of the onboarding for new hires.
• In 2016/2017 changes were made to the existing front counter in the Corporate Services
Department and the Human Services Department which included lowering a section of the
counter and creating space for someone to be seated
• In 2017 the Accessible Maintenance Procedure for the preventative and emergency
maintenance of the accessible elements in public spaces was approved and added to the
Multi-Year Accessibility Plan 2015-2018
• In 2017 procedures for the Temporary Disruptions when accessible elements required are
not in working order was approved and added to the Multi-Year Accessibility Plan 2015-2018
• An accessible central reception space was created on the main floor in the Atrium at the
County Administration Centre
• The Bruce County Museum & Cultural Centre installed automatic door openers for the
washrooms.
• The public washrooms on the 2nd floor at the County Administration Centre were retrofitted
in 2019 with push button entrances, accessible sinks and counters.
• The existing push button entrance into the Council Chambers was updated in 2019 to allow
both doors to open at the same time, including the installation of a new push button.

Message from Mayor French, Warden
Marks, and Mayor Preston
On behalf of the Community Safety and Well-Being Plan Coordinating Committee,
we are pleased to present the Aylmer-Elgin-St. Thomas Community Safety and
Well-being (CSWB) Plan. The CSWB Plan is a roadmap for how partners across
different sectors can work together to make our community a safer, more inclusive
place where all residents thrive. This plan marks a shift in focus from a reactive,
response-based approach to incidents to a more proactive, holistic approach to
community safety.
With this plan, we will respond to the needs of our communities as we use local data
to make evidence-informed decisions. We will develop and implement new
strategies to address the complex issues facing our communities, and we will work
with our community partners to rethink the way we deliver services. Many of our
community partners are already doing excellent work to contribute to safety and
well-being in Aylmer, Elgin and St. Thomas. The CSWB Plan recognizes that complex
risks to safety and well-being cannot be addressed in isolation by any one
organization, agency or sector. The goal of this Plan is to achieve greater
coordination and collaboration on issues and situations before they escalate. It is
important to continue to build and strengthen partnerships across sectors, and we
thank our many community partners that have come together to develop this Plan.
This Plan will define community safety and well-being planning in Elgin and St.
Thomas over the coming years, but it is not a final destination. Community safety and
well-being issues will continue to evolve, and we are committed to ongoing
engagement and dialogue to ensure that the Plan remains informed, relevant and
reflective of evolving needs. We thank you for your feedback throughout the
planning process, and we look forward to working with you all to make our
communities safer, more inclusive places where all residents thrive.
Mary French Tom Marks Joe Preston
Mayor, Town of Aylmer Warden, County of Elgin Mayor, City of St. Thomas

Community Safety and Well-Being
Planning In Ontario: An Overview
In 2009, the work of community safety and well-being planning began in Ontario with a
partnership between the Ministry of the Solicitor General and the Ontario Association of
Chiefs of Police. Community safety and well-being is broader than the traditional
definition of safety (i.e. crime) and is critical to ensure that community members are
safe, have a sense of belonging, have opportunities to participate, and are able to meet
their needs for education, health care, food, housing, income, and social and cultural
expression. Ensuring this sense of safety and well-being requires a multi sector,
‐
collaborative effort.
The Police Services Act (1990) mandates every municipal council to prepare and adopt
a Community Safety and Well-Being (CSWB) Plan. Under the legislation, municipalities
have the discretion and flexibility to develop joint plans with surrounding municipalities.
The municipalities in Aylmer-Elgin-St. Thomas are working collaboratively to develop a
shared Community Safety and Well-Being Plan for all of Elgin.
As part of the legislation, the Province has mandated a number of requirements.
Municipalities must:
Prepare and adopt a Community Safety and Well-Being Plan
Work in partnership with a multi-sectoral advisory committee comprised of
representation from the police service board and other local service providers in
health/mental health, education, community/social services and children/youth
services
Conduct consultations with the advisory committee and members of the public
The Ontario Framework
The Ontario Community Safety and Well-Being Planning framework operated as a guide
in developing the Aylmer-Elgin-St. Thomas Community Safety and Well-Being Plan. This
framework focuses on collaboration, information sharing and performance
measurement, and identifies four areas in which communities can be made safer and
healthier:
1. Social Development
2. Prevention
3. Risk Intervention
4. Incident Response

Phase 1: Project Planning and Onboarding
At the initiation of the planning for the Aylmer-Elgin-St. Thomas Community Safety
and Well-Being Plan, a kick off meeting was held with the Coordinating Committee.
In addition to this, an introductory video was produced and shared with the Advisory
Committee members. The video can be found here.
Phase 2: Research and Asset Mapping
The second phase of the community safety and well-being planning process
focused on collecting local data and information about the communities in Aylmer-
Elgin-St. Thomas. This is a key component in the creation of the Community Safety
and Well-Being Plan as it provides a snapshot, that is based on data, about what is
happening in the areas of health, well-being and safety in the Elgin region.
Our Approach
Inventory of Planning Tables
An inventory of existing planning tables in Aylmer-Elgin-St. Thomas was also
conducted. A total of 20 planning tables were identified. This inventory highlighted:
The purpose of the planning table
A high level description of the organizations that participate on the planning table
A list of the strategies, projects or other current work of the planning table,
including any research/reports conducted by the planning table
This inventory helped to ensure the Community Safety and Well-Being Plan did not
duplicate existing work and, instead, leveraged the current planning tables in Aylmer-
Elgin-St. Thomas and the work that they are doing.
Local Data
A key aspect in the development of the Aylmer-Elgin-St. Thomas Community Safety
and Well-Being Plan is making sure the plan is evidence-informed. To ensure this,
local data was collected to validate resident perceptions, to support ongoing
discussions related to safety and well-being, and to create a foundation from which
to monitor and evaluate the Community Safety and Well-Being Plan work as it
moves into implementation. A Data Package was developed to support this process.
It can be found here.
Phase 3: Community Engagement
The third phase of the community safety and well-being planning process focused
on community engagement. Throughout this phase we engaged with residents and
community organizations in Aylmer-Elgin-St. Thomas to collect information about
their perceptions of community safety and well-being. This is a key component in
the creation of the Community Safety and Well-Being Plan as it reveals how
residents feel about the communities in which they live.

Subject: Proclamations
Policy Number: 035
Approval Date: October 3, 2017
Approved By: Resolution Number R16-10-428
Prepared By: Director of Corporate Services
1.00 Objective
Proclamations provide a means for Council to promote public awareness campaigns,
charitable fundraising campaigns, arts and cultural celebrations of significance to the Town of
Essex. Proclamations may also acknowledge special honours for individuals and organizations
of the Town of Essex in recognition of a special achievement. Accordingly, it is important that
Council’s endorsement of proclamations is based on a framework that ensures all requests are
dealt with consistently.
2.00 Purpose
The purpose of this Policy is to establish the framework for Council endorsement of
proclamations.
3.00 Scope
This policy applies to all requests for proclamations received by the Town of Essex.
1
4.00 Definitions
In this policy:
“Chief Administrative Officer” means the individual appointed as the Chief Administrative
Officer for the Town of Essex;
“Clerk” means the Clerk of the Town of Essex;
“Council” means the Council of The Corporation of the Town of Essex, comprised of the
Mayor, Deputy Mayor and Councillors;
“Flag Raising” for purposes of this policy, means the raising of a flag in conjunction with a
proclamation that has been endorsed by Council;
“Proclamation” means a public or official announcement, particularly one dealing with a
matter of great importance that may be endorsed by Council of the Town of Essex and may
be recognized on a particular day, week or month; and
“Regular Council Meeting” means a scheduled meeting held at regular intervals in
accordance with the approved calendar/schedule of meetings and the Town’s Procedural By-
Law.
5.00 Proclamation Criteria
Proclamations that are of significance to the Town of Essex may be endorsed by Council of
the Town of Essex for the following:
a) Civic promotions;
b) Public awareness campaigns;
c) Charitable fundraising campaigns;
d) Arts and cultural celebrations; or
e) Special honours for individuals and organizations for special achievements.
2
Only proclamations that involve participation by the Town of Essex or its residents will be
considered for endorsement.
Proclamations will not be endorsed by Council of the Town of Essex for the following:
a) Matters of political controversy;
b) Controversial matters which may be subject to opposing points of view (for
example, “Right to Life” Movement);
c) Religious organizations or religious events or celebrations;
d) Individual conviction;
e) Organizations or events with no direct relationship to the Town of Essex and/or do
not involve participation by the Town of Essex or its residents;
f) Celebrations, campaigns or events contrary to Town policies or by-laws;
g) Celebrations, campaigns or events intended for profit-making purposes; or
h) Matters attempting to influence government policy.
6.00 Submitting a Proclamation Request
All organizations or persons submitting a request for a proclamation must complete a
Proclamation Request Form attached as Appendix A to this policy. Proclamation Request
Forms shall be submitted to the attention of the Clerk.
The following limitations related to proclamation requests are noted for those submitting a
request:
a) An organization may only request one proclamation annually;
b) A organization does not have exclusive rights to the day, week or month of their
proclamation; and
c) Proclamations on a similar topic will be issued on a first come, first served basis;
and
d) Multi-year proclamations or proclamations that are to be repeated indefinitely will
not be considered and must be requested on an annual basis. (There is no
3
requirement to submit a Proclamation Request annually for multi-year
proclamations that were endorsed by Council prior to the implementation of this
policy.)
7.00 Proclamations with Flag Raising
Proclamation Requests that include a flag raising may be permitted provided the
proclamation request is in accordance with Section 5.00, Proclamation Criteria and that the
flag raising does not conflict with the Rules for Flying the National Flag of Canada or any other
flag being flown by the Town of Essex.
8.00 Review of Proclamation Requests
Proclamation requests will be reviewed by the Clerk against the eligibility criteria noted in this
Policy. In the event that the request does not comply with this policy, the Clerk, in
consultation with the Chief Administrative Officer, will not include the request on a Council
meeting agenda and will advise the Mayor and organization/person submitting the request
accordingly. Proclamation requests that meet all eligibility criteria will be placed on the
agenda for the next Regular Council Meeting under the “Correspondence” section of the
agenda.
9.00 Council Endorsement of Proclamation Requests
Proclamations will not be read aloud at Council Meetings and shall only be considered at
Regular Council Meetings.
Following consideration of a Proclamation Request by Council, the Clerk will advise the
organization/person who submitted the Proclamation Request Form in writing of the
outcome of Council’s consideration. Proclamations that have been endorsed by Council will
be noted on the “Proclamations” page of the Town’s website and will remain listed for a
period ending on December 31st of the year in which the proclamation was endorsed.
4
Items such as decals, signs, banners, brochures, or similar items that accompany a
proclamation request will not be displayed at Town facilities unless, at the sole discretion of
the Clerk, it is determined that they provide information of significant value to residents of
the Town of Essex.

 Auto Mayors Motion

WHEREAS the Auto Mayors work collaboratively at the provincial and federal orders of government to promote awareness, advocacy and strategic policy initiatives that strengthen the Canadian economy through advancements and investments in the automotive sector;

WHEREAS continued progress toward tariff-free access to the U.S. market and maintaining an integrated North American auto sector remain the auto sector’s top priority;

WHEREAS the Auto Mayors welcome ongoing collaboration with the Province and the Federal government on greenhouse gas regulations and electrification targets and policies that reflect current market demand, infrastructure readiness and alignment with the U.S.;

WHEREAS the Auto Mayors are ready to work with Federal partners on a coordinated approach to global competition that ensures Canada remains an attractive destination for investment;

WHEREAS strengthening domestic production requires aligning tariff remission frameworks with manufacturing levels and strengthening Buy Ontario procurement policies to ensure public sector fleet purchasing continues to support Ontario based manufacturers;

AND WHEREAS regular review and monitoring of industrial electricity rates, including how domestic rates compare to export rates, will help ensure Ontario manufacturers remain competitive and positioned for growth.

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the City of Peterborough, as a member of the Auto Mayors Caucus, support the Auto Mayors’ continued efforts to highlight the automotive sector’s local economic impact, including jobs, supply chains, and community stability, while supporting the automotive ecosystem through business retention and economic development efforts;

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the City of Peterborough joins with the Auto Mayors to support the Federal government’s ongoing efforts in the Canada-U.S. trade negotiations to protect and secure the long-term prosperity of Canada’s automotive industry;

SHORT TITLE
This By-law shall be cited as the Procedure By-law.
PART 1 - GENERAL
1.0 DEFINITIONS
For the purpose of this By-law:
"Business Sections" means the divisions within a regular Committee of the Whole
meeting each dedicated to specific subject matters within the scope and responsibility of
Council;
"Business Section Chair" means the person appointed by Council to preside during
their respective section at a regular Committee of the Whole meeting;
"Business Section Vice-Chair" means the person appointed by Council who would
preside over the proceedings of their respective section at a regular Committee of the
Whole meeting in the absence of the Chair;
"Chair" means the person appointed by Council or a Committee to preside at a
meeting;
"Chief Administrative Officer" means the Chief Administrative Officer of the
Corporation of the County of Simcoe;
"Clerk" means the County Clerk of the Corporation of the County of Simcoe or their
designate;
“Closed Session” means a meeting or a part of a meeting which is not open to the
public in accordance with the Municipal Act;
"Committee" means any Committee of Council or similar body of which at least 50 per
cent of the members are also members of one or more councils or local boards, and
includes the Committee of the Whole, Special or Ad Hoc Committees, Advisory
Committees or a Task Force of Council;
"Committee of the Whole" means all members of Council and appointed members
sitting as a Committee for the purpose of conducting business in a less formal manner
in accordance with this By-Law;
"Confirmatory By-law" means a By-law passed for the purpose of giving general effect
to the decisions or proceedings of Council;
Page 4 of 57
"Consent Items" means items placed in a section of the agenda that is used to adopt
items with one motion. Consent items may be pulled from the list of consent items by
any member, for further discussion, debate or motion;
"Council" means the Council of the Corporation of the County of Simcoe;
"Delegation" means an address to Council or a Committee at the request of a person
or an organization wishing to speak;
"Deputy Warden" means the person elected by Council to fulfill the duties of Head of
Council in the Warden's absence, and to support the Warden under their guidance and
direction;
“Electronic Meeting” means a meeting held in whole or in part by videoconference, or
other form of electronic means;
"Head of Council" means the Warden for the County of Simcoe or any member acting
in the capacity of the Warden;
"Majority Vote" means an affirmative vote of more than one half of the members
present and eligible to vote;
"Meeting" means any regular, special, or other meeting of Council, or of a Local Board
or a Committee of either of them where, a quorum is present and where members
discuss or otherwise deal with any matter in a way that materially advances the
business or decision-making of the Council, Local Board or Committee;
"Member" means a member of Council, a member of Committee or an alternate
member of Council appointed by a lower-tier municipality under Section 268 of the
Municipal Act;
"Motion" means a proposal by a member presented in a meeting, in accordance with
the rules of procedure, to deal with a matter before Council or Committee;
"Presentation" means an address to Council or Committee that has the consent of the
Warden or Chair and was arranged at the request of Council, Committee or staff, and
may include the presenting of an award, certificate, cheque, etc.;
"Quorum" means the number of members required to be present at a meeting to
validate the transaction of business, that number being more than half of the members
of the Council or Committee who are eligible to vote;
Page 5 of 57
"Recess" means a short intermission in meeting proceedings which does not close the
meeting, and after which business will immediately be resumed at exactly the point in
proceedings where it was stopped;
"Recorded Vote" means a written record of the name and vote of every member
present, voting on any matter or question at a Council meeting;
"Resolution" means the decision of Council on any motion;
"Two-thirds Majority Vote" means an affirmative vote of at least two-thirds of the
members present and eligible to vote at a meeting. Weighted vote shall not apply to
decisions where this By-law requires a two-thirds majority vote;
"Vice-Chair" means the person appointed by Council or Committee who would preside
over the proceedings of a Committee meeting in the absence of the Chair;
"Weighted Vote" refers to a vote where the number of votes allocated to members of
Council is prescribed by County By-law and is a written record of the name and vote of
every member present, voting on any matter or question. A weighted vote shall only
occur in a meeting of Council upon request and must be requested only prior to a matter
or question being put.
2.0 APPLICATION/INTERPRETATION
2.1 Application
The rules of procedure contained in this By-law, or any standing or special rules of
order adopted by the Corporation of the County of Simcoe shall be observed in all
proceedings of Council and, with necessary modifications, its Committees and
Boards. Failure to strictly adhere to the rules of procedure contained in this By-law
shall not invalidate the action(s) of Council or a Committee acting in good faith.
2.2 Statutes Affecting By-law
Whenever any reference is made in this By-law to a statute of the Legislature of the
Province of Ontario, such reference shall be deemed to include all subsequent
amendments to such statute and all successor legislation to such statute.
2.3 Matters Not Specifically Provided for in this By-law
Matters not specifically provided for in this By-law shall be decided by the Warden or
Chair, in accordance with as far as practicable, parliamentary procedures as
generally outlined in "Robert's Rules of Order''. The Clerk may be called upon to
provide advice regarding procedural matters. Following receipt of any advice from
the Clerk, the Warden or Chair shall announce their ruling.
Page 6 of 57
2.4 Notice Required for Amendment or Repeal of By-law
This By-law, or any part thereof, shall not be amended or repealed at any meeting of
Council unless notice of the proposed amendment or repeal has been given at a
previous meeting of Council. The requirement to give this notice shall not be waived.
2.5 Suspension of the Rules of this By-Law
Except for statutory provisions or unless otherwise provided for within this By-law,
any provision of this By-law may be suspended in whole or in part by Council on
obtaining not less than two-thirds majority vote and weighted vote shall not apply.
2.6 Statutory Requirements
Notwithstanding anything in this By-law, where Council or a Committee convenes for
the purpose of holding a hearing as required by any statute or By-law, the provisions
of the statute and the Statutory Powers Procedure Act, as applicable, shall govern
the proceedings. If there is found to be any conflict between this By-law and any
statute or By-law, the provisions of the statute or By-law shall prevail.
2.7 Schedules
Schedules 1, 2 and 3 to this By-law shall form part of this By-law.
2.8 Severability
If any section or part of this By-law is found by any court of competent jurisdiction to
be invalid, such section or part shall be deemed to be severable and shall not affect
the validity or enforceability of any other provisions of this By-law or the By-law as a
whole.
PART 2 - DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES AND POWERS
3.0 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF COUNCIL
3.1 Role of Council
In accordance with the Municipal Act, it is the role of Council:
a) to represent the citizens of Simcoe County and to consider the well-being and
interests of the County;
b) to develop and evaluate the policies and programs of the County;
c) to determine which services the County provides;
d) to ensure that administrative policies, practices and procedures and controllership
policies, practices and procedures are in place to implement the decisions of
County Council;
e) to ensure the accountability and transparency of the operations of the County,
including the activities of the senior management of the County; and
f) to maintain the financial integrity of the County; and
g) to carry out the duties of the County Council under the Municipal Act or any other
Act.
Page 7 of 57
4.0 CONDUCT OF MEMBERS
4.1 Respectful Conduct
Members in attendance at meetings shall conduct themselves with decorum in
accordance with the provisions of this By-law and in a manner that demonstrates
professionalism and fosters respect and recognition for the formal nature of such
proceedings.
4.2 Right to Participate
Members shall have the right to full participation in the proceedings of Council
unless prohibited by law or as otherwise prescribed in this By-law.
4.3 Restrictions
Unless otherwise prescribed in the Municipal Act, no member shall:
a) be absent from the meetings of Council for three successive months without
authorization by way of resolution of Council;
b) speak disrespectfully of the Reigning Sovereign, or of any member of the Royal
Family, the Governor General, the Lieutenant Governor of any Province, any
member municipality, any other Council member or any official or employee of
the County;
c) use indecent, offensive or insulting language in or against Council or any
member;
d) engage in private conversation while in a Council meeting or use electronic
